label: Bonus Class 3
title: The Question Machine
bigIdea: English builds a question by moving a helper verb (is, are, can) in front of the subject; if there is no helper, it calls do or does. Arabic just adds هل or changes the tone.
bigIdeaAr: تصنع الإنجليزية السؤال بنقل فعل مساعد (is, are, can) إلى ما قبل الفاعل، وإن لم يوجد فعل مساعد تستدعي do أو does. أما العربية فتضيف هل أو تغيّر نغمة الصوت فقط.
builtOn: Bonus Class 2: English statement order S-V-O
Lessons 1-3: Present Simple with do/does in negatives (I don't, she doesn't)
Lesson 9: can / can't for ability (Can you skate?)
Lesson 10: Wh- questions (who, what, where, when, why, how) and mystery words (clue, riddle, hint, suspect)
Lessons 11-12: comparatives (faster, better) and a / an / the (the new kid, a newcomer)

objectives.en: I can turn a statement into a yes/no question by moving the helper (Noor is shy -> Is Noor shy?).
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أحوّل الجملة الخبرية إلى سؤال بنعم أو لا بنقل الفعل المساعد (Noor is shy ← Is Noor shy?).

objectives.en: I can use do / does when there is no helper, and remove the -s from the main verb (Does she play...?).
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أستعمل do / does عندما لا يوجد فعل مساعد، وأحذف -s من الفعل الأساسي (Does she play...?).

objectives.en: I can build Wh- questions in the right order: Wh- + helper + subject + verb.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أبني أسئلة Wh- بالترتيب الصحيح: أداة الاستفهام + الفعل المساعد + الفاعل + الفعل.

objectives.en: I can use rising and falling intonation and compare English questions with Arabic هل questions.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أستعمل النغمة الصاعدة والهابطة، وأقارن الأسئلة الإنجليزية بأسئلة هل في العربية.

keyTerms.meaning: A small verb that helps the main verb and can move in questions: am, is, are, can, do, does.
Swapping the subject and the helper to make a question: You can swim -> Can you swim?
Adding do / does to make a question or negative when the sentence has no helper.
A question you answer with yes or no: Can you code?
A question that asks for information: Where do you hang out?
The music of the voice: going up or down at the end of a sentence.

linguisticsCorner.title: How the world's languages ask questions

facts.en: Languages ask yes/no questions in a few main ways: a question word or particle (Arabic هل, Chinese ma, Japanese ka, Turkish mi), a special verb ending, intonation alone (the voice goes up), or changing the word order (English, German).
facts.ar: تطرح اللغات السؤال الذي جوابه نعم أو لا بطرق رئيسية قليلة: أداة استفهام (هل في العربية، و ma في الصينية، و ka في اليابانية، و mi في التركية)، أو لاحقة خاصة في الفعل، أو النغمة وحدها (يرتفع الصوت)، أو تغيير ترتيب الكلمات (الإنجليزية والألمانية).

facts.en: The particle method is the most common in the world. Changing the word order, as English does, is rare (it is found mostly in European languages), and English 'do-support' (a helper with no meaning of its own) is rarer still.
facts.ar: طريقة أداة الاستفهام هي الأكثر انتشاراً في العالم. أما قلب الترتيب كما في الإنجليزية فنادر (يوجد غالباً في لغات أوروبية)، واستدعاء do (فعل مساعد بلا معنى خاص به) أندر من ذلك.

facts.en: English did not always use do. About 400 years ago, in Shakespeare's time, people could still ask without do: 'What say you?' (a real Shakespeare line) or 'Know you the way?'. Do was already used too, and over the next century or so it became the normal helper: Do you know the way? What do you say?
facts.ar: لم تكن الإنجليزية تستعمل do دائماً. قبل نحو 400 سنة، في زمن شكسبير، كان الناس ما زالوا يسألون أحياناً بدونها: 'What say you?' (من كلام شكسبير) أو 'Know you the way?'. وكانت do مستعملة أيضاً، ثم صارت خلال القرن التالي تقريباً هي الفعل المساعد المعتاد: Do you know the way?

facts.en: In many languages, including English and Arabic, the voice often rises at the end of a yes/no question. In English, Wh- questions often fall at the end. These are tendencies, not strict rules. Intonation is grammar you hear, not grammar you see.
facts.ar: في لغات كثيرة، ومنها الإنجليزية والعربية، يرتفع الصوت غالباً في آخر السؤال الذي جوابه نعم أو لا. وفي الإنجليزية تنخفض النغمة غالباً في آخر أسئلة Wh-. وهذه ميول عامة لا قواعد صارمة. التنغيم قواعد نسمعها ولا نراها.

arabicBridge.point: Arabic adds هل and keeps the statement order. English adds no word: it moves is to the front. (And remember Bonus Class 1: Arabic has no is here at all.)
arabicBridge.pointAr: العربية تضيف هل وتُبقي ترتيب الجملة كما هو، أما الإنجليزية فلا تضيف كلمة بل تنقل is إلى البداية. (وتذكّر الحصة الإضافية 1: لا يوجد في العربية فعل مقابل is هنا أصلاً.)

arabicBridge.arabic: هل تستطيع أن تسبح؟ / تعرف تسبح؟ (عامية)
arabicBridge.point: English moves can before you. In spoken Arabic, the tone alone can make the question; English needs the helper in front.
arabicBridge.pointAr: الإنجليزية تنقل can قبل you. في العامية قد تكفي النغمة وحدها لصنع السؤال، أما الإنجليزية فتحتاج إلى الفعل المساعد في البداية.

arabicBridge.point: هل has no meaning of its own; it only says 'this is a question'. English do in a question works in a similar way: a helper with no meaning of its own (but it carries the -s and the time).
arabicBridge.pointAr: هل لا معنى خاصاً لها، فهي تقول فقط 'هذا سؤال'. و do في السؤال الإنجليزي تعمل بالطريقة نفسها تقريباً: مساعد سؤال بلا معنى.

arabicBridge.point: Arabic: question word + verb. English: question word + do + subject + verb. The do is invisible in Arabic, so students forget it.
arabicBridge.pointAr: العربية: أداة الاستفهام + الفعل. الإنجليزية: أداة الاستفهام + do + الفاعل + الفعل. لا يوجد في العربية ما يقابل do هنا، لذلك ينساها الطلاب.

arabicBridge.point: Arabic puts the verb right after ماذا. English needs does, and the main verb is mean, not means.
arabicBridge.pointAr: في العربية يأتي الفعل بعد ماذا مباشرة، أما في الإنجليزية فنحتاج إلى does ويصبح الفعل mean بلا -s.

arabicBridge.point: Same pattern! When who is the subject (the doer), English uses no do, just like Arabic.
arabicBridge.pointAr: النمط نفسه! عندما تكون who هي الفاعل لا تستعمل الإنجليزية do، تماماً كالعربية.

commonErrors.right: Where do you go after school?
commonErrors.why: Copy of أين تذهب؟ Arabic has no word for do in questions.
Copy of the Arabic statement order with question tone. Native speakers say this only to show surprise or check; a normal question moves can to the front.
The helper stays in statement order. After the Wh- word, the helper must jump before the subject.
The -s moves to does: does takes it, and the main verb goes back to its base form.
he / she / it need does, just like doesn't in negatives (Lesson 3).
Copy of ماذا تعني؟ The verb comes straight after the question word in Arabic; English needs does first.

teacher: Bonus Class 3 slides with the Question Machine: a slot diagram [Wh-] [HELPER] [SUBJECT] [VERB] [REST]
Helper cards: am, is, are, can, do, does (the helper cards in yellow)
Intonation arrows (up and down) on the slide
Jeopardy board slide with 4 categories x 4 values
A 'mystery object' picture hidden behind a box on the slide (for 20 Questions)
student: Paper and the color pens from Bonus Class 1 (add yellow for helpers)
Two paper cards: an up arrow and a down arrow
Six small cards they write in class: is, are, can, do, does, ?

stages.name: Warm-up: 20 Questions with Lumi
stages.method: Guessing game (authentic need to ask questions)
stages.purpose: Get students asking questions freely so the teacher can collect their real question forms, correct and incorrect.
teacherSays: Lumi has a mystery object in this box. You can ask yes/no questions only. I answer yes or no.
Ready? Ask me anything! Is it big? Can you eat it? Go!
(Write every student question on the slide exactly as they say it, even the broken ones.)
You found it! Now look at all your questions. Some are perfect, some are... interesting. Today we build a Question Machine so every question comes out perfect.
teacherSaysAr: اسألوا أسئلة جوابها نعم أو لا فقط.
انظروا إلى أسئلتكم: بعضها ممتاز وبعضها يحتاج إلى إصلاح. اليوم نبني آلة أسئلة.
studentsDo: Ask yes/no questions to find the mystery object (a backpack, a medal or a phone charger).
Look at the list of their own questions on the slide.
tips: Do not correct during the game. Write the questions down; they become the material for the Discovery stage.
Typical forms you will collect: 'It is big?', 'You can eat it?', 'Is it blue?' - perfect contrast material.

stages.name: Discovery: How the Question Machine Works
stages.method: Guided discovery (find-the-rule) with a slot diagram and moving helper cards
stages.purpose: Students discover inversion: the helper jumps over the subject in yes/no and Wh- questions.
teacherSays: Look at the pairs. Statement: 'Noor is nervous.' Question: 'Is Noor nervous?' What moved? ... Is! Where did it go? ... In front of Noor!
Another: 'Ziad can code.' -> 'Can Ziad code?' Same thing! The yellow helper jumps over the subject.
'They are friendly.' -> ? ... 'Are they friendly?' Perfect.
Now Wh- questions. Put the Wh- word at the very front, then the machine works the same: 'Where is the gym?' 'What can Omar bake?'
The machine has five slots: Wh-word, helper, subject, verb, rest. The Wh- slot can be empty for yes/no questions.
Now go back to our 20 Questions list. 'It is big?' - fix it with the machine! ... 'Is it big?'
teacherSaysAr: ما الكلمة التي تحركت؟ الفعل المساعد قفز فوق الفاعل!
في أسئلة Wh- نضع أداة الاستفهام أولاً، ثم تعمل الآلة بالطريقة نفسها.
studentsDo: Compare statement/question pairs and say what moved.
Move the yellow helper card in front of the subject on paper (or tell the teacher where to drag it).
Fix their own warm-up questions using the machine.

exercise.instructions: Make a question. Move the helper in front of the subject. (Wh- word given in brackets.)
exercise.instructionsAr: كوّن سؤالاً بنقل الفعل المساعد قبل الفاعل. (أداة الاستفهام بين القوسين.)

items.prompt: They are in the science lab.
items.answer: Are they in the science lab?

tips: Physically moving the helper card is the key: it makes inversion visible. If students cannot control slides, they say 'move is to the front!'
Point out that in these questions the helper comes right after the Wh- word: Wh- + helper + subject.

stages.name: The Helper Who Appears: Do and Does
stages.nameAr: المساعد الذي يظهر فجأة: do و does
stages.purpose: Discover that when there is no helper, English calls do / does, and the -s moves from the verb to does.
teacherSays: Problem! 'You like riddles.' Where's the yellow helper? ... There isn't one! Like is the main verb. Can we move like? 'Like you riddles?' ... Sounds like Shakespeare!
So the machine calls a helper: DO. 'Do you like riddles?'
Now: 'Sara plays tennis.' The machine calls does for she. And look at plays... the -s jumps onto does! 'Does Sara play tennis?'
Only one -s here: does takes it, play goes back to normal.
Same in Wh- questions: 'Where do you hang out?' 'What does Hamad collect?'
You already know this helper! Lesson 3: I don't, she doesn't. Do and does work in negatives and questions.
teacherSaysAr: لا يوجد فعل مساعد؟ الآلة تستدعي do. ومع he / she / it تستدعي does.
حرف -s ينتقل إلى does، ويعود الفعل الأساسي إلى أصله.
studentsDo: Try to move the main verb, notice it sounds wrong, then add do / does.
Show the 'do' or 'does' card for each subject the teacher says (I, she, they, my cousin, Omar and Ziad).
Complete the exercise and read each question aloud.

exercise.instructions: Make a question. Choose is, are, can, do or does. Watch the -s!
exercise.instructionsAr: كوّن سؤالاً. اختر is أو are أو can أو do أو does، وانتبه لحرف -s!

items.answer: Do your cousins live near school?
Why do they need a hint?

tips: If a student says 'Does she plays?', point at the -s and say 'does already has the -s!'
Challenge for fast finishers: 'Who won the race?' Why is there no do? (who is the subject; see Arabic Bridge).
Keep the 'Shakespeare' joke: 'Like you riddles?' sounds old because English really worked like this about 400 years ago (Early Modern English, not 'Old English', which is much older).

stages.name: Linguistics Corner: How the World Asks
stages.purpose: Broaden general knowledge: particles, intonation and inversion across languages, and the history of do.
teacherSays: Languages have a few main tools to ask: a question word like هل, the voice going up, or moving words around.
Arabic uses هل. Chinese adds ma at the end. Japanese adds ka. English? Moves the helper!
The particle tool is the most common in the world. English's do-helper is quite rare - you are learning an unusual system.
And English didn't always use do! In Shakespeare's time, about 400 years ago, people could say 'What say you?' Today: 'What do you say?'
teacherSaysAr: اللغات تسأل بأدوات رئيسية، منها: أداة استفهام مثل هل، أو رفع الصوت، أو تحريك الكلمات.
استعمال do في الأسئلة نادر بين لغات العالم، وفي زمن شكسبير قبل نحو 400 سنة كان الناس يسألون أحياناً بدونها.
studentsDo: Decide which tool each example uses.
Turn two Shakespeare-style questions into modern English.

exercise.instructions: Which tool makes the question? Write: particle, intonation or word order. For the 400-year-old questions, write the modern question.
exercise.instructionsAr: ما الأداة التي تصنع السؤال؟ اكتب: أداة استفهام أو نغمة أو ترتيب. وللأسئلة القديمة (زمن شكسبير) اكتب السؤال الحديث.

items.prompt: Chinese: Ni hao ma? (You good ma?)
Shakespeare's time: Know you the answer?

tips: Keep it light; the history is a hook, not a test.
'English uses inversion' is also true in German (Spielst du?) - mention if a student knows German or French.

stages.name: Arabic Bridge and Voice Music: هل vs the Machine
stages.nameAr: جسر العربية وموسيقى الصوت: هل مقابل الآلة
stages.method: Contrastive analysis + intonation drill with arrow cards
stages.purpose: Translate Arabic questions using the machine, and practice rising (yes/no) and falling (Wh-) intonation.
teacherSays: Arabic: هل + the normal sentence. Nothing moves. English: the helper moves or do appears.
Interesting: هل has no meaning of its own - it only says 'question!'. English do in a question is similar: a helper with no meaning of its own.
Careful with أين الصالة الرياضية؟ - no verb in Arabic. English needs is: Where IS the gym? Bonus Class 1 again!
Now the music. Yes/no questions usually go UP at the end: Can you SWIM? (arrow up). Wh- questions usually go DOWN: Where do you LIVE? (arrow down).
Show me your arrow when I say a question!
teacherSaysAr: العربية تضع هل قبل الجملة ولا تحرّك شيئاً، والإنجليزية تحرّك الفعل المساعد أو تستدعي do.
أسئلة نعم/لا ترتفع نغمتها في الآخر غالباً، وأسئلة Wh- تنخفض غالباً.
studentsDo: Translate Arabic questions into English with the machine.
Hold up the up or down arrow for each question the teacher reads.
Read their own translations with the right arrow.

exercise.instructions: Say it in English, then show the arrow: up or down.
exercise.instructionsAr: قلها بالإنجليزية ثم ارفع السهم: صاعد أم هابط.

items.answer: Is the new kid friendly? (or: Is the new student friendly?) (up)
Who won the medal? (down; no do - who is the subject)

tips: Be honest about intonation: 'usually', not 'always'. Wh- questions can rise when you are surprised or being extra friendly.
Item 8 uses won (past) - students know 'won' from Lesson 11 vocabulary context; accept 'Who has the medal?' too.
Exaggerate the voice music at first, then make it natural.

stages.name: Team Jeopardy: Here's the Answer, What's the Question?
stages.nameAr: تحدي الفرق: هذا هو الجواب، فما السؤال؟
stages.purpose: Produce accurate questions under game pressure, choosing the right helper and order.
teacherSays: Jeopardy time! Four categories: Can-Do, Crew Facts, Mystery and Race Day. 10 to 40 points.
I show you the ANSWER. You give me the QUESTION. Perfect question = full points. Right idea but a broken machine = half points, and the other team can steal by fixing it!
Team Lumi chooses first. Which category and how many points?
teacherSaysAr: أعرض عليكم الجواب، وأنتم تقولون السؤال.
السؤال الصحيح تماماً = كل النقاط. وإذا كان فيه خطأ يمكن للفريق الآخر أن يسرق النقاط بإصلاحه.
studentsDo: Agree on the question with their teammate (15 seconds) and say it with the right intonation.
Steal points by fixing the other team's broken question.

exercise.instructions: Here is the answer. Say the question. (Model questions below; other correct questions are fine.)
exercise.instructionsAr: هذا هو الجواب، فما السؤال؟ (أسئلة نموذجية أدناه، وتُقبل أسئلة صحيحة أخرى.)

items.prompt: Can-Do 10: Yes, I can. I can swim fast.
Can-Do 20: No, she can't. Sara can't juggle.
Crew Facts 10: Yes, he does. Omar likes memes.
Crew Facts 20: We hang out at the mall.
Mystery 20: The suspect is the man in the black jacket.
Mystery 30: It means a small clue.
Mystery 40: Because she has a new secret.
items.answer: Why is she happy? / Why does she smile? (any logical Why question)

items.prompt: Race Day 20: Yes, he is. Ziad is faster than Omar.
Race Day 40: The race starts at nine o'clock.
items.answer: When does the race start? / What time does the race start?

tips: Short answers (Yes, he does / No, she can't) are a gift: the helper in the answer tells you the helper for the question. Teach this trick if students struggle.
With 2 students, play student vs student; with 1 student, student vs Lumi (the teacher plays Lumi and sometimes gives broken questions to steal).
40-point items accept any logical question; reward creativity.

stages.name: Exit Ticket, Did You Know? and Mission
stages.purpose: Check each student's question building individually and send them home with a fact.
teacherSays: Exit ticket: five questions to build, alone, in a private chat.

Did you know? Small children learning English as their first language also say 'Where you going?' and 'Why he is sad?' for a while. Some of your mistakes are the same ones young English-speaking children make - it's a natural step!
Your mission: interview someone at home with 5 English questions: one with is, one with can, one with do, one with does and one Wh- question.
teacherSaysAr: هل تعلم؟ الأطفال الصغار الذين يتعلمون الإنجليزية لغةً أولى يقولون أيضاً 'Where you going?' لفترة من الوقت. أخطاؤك مرحلة طبيعية!
مهمتك: اسأل أحداً في البيت خمسة أسئلة بالإنجليزية.
studentsDo: Build 5 questions in a private chat.
Read one question aloud with the right intonation.
tips: Note who still uses 'Where you...?' and add one question-building warm-up to Lessons 13-14.
The child-language fact is well documented (children go through stages of non-inverted questions); it lowers anxiety about errors.

items.prompt: Fix it: Where you meet your friends?
items.answer: Where do you meet your friends?

items.prompt: Fix it: Why the new kid is nervous?
items.answer: Why is the new kid nervous?

homework.en: Interview Mission: ask someone at home 5 English questions (is, can, do, does, and a Wh- question). Write the questions and their answers. Then write a 5-question riddle about a mystery object for the next class.
homework.ar: مهمة المقابلة: اسأل أحداً في البيت خمسة أسئلة بالإنجليزية (is و can و do و does وسؤال Wh-) واكتب الأسئلة وإجاباتها. ثم اكتب لغزاً من 5 أسئلة عن شيء غامض للحصة القادمة.
tasks: Write 5 interview questions and the answers.
Color the helper yellow and the subject blue in each question.
Prepare a mystery object for a 20 Questions game in Lesson 13.

support: Work with is and can only first; add do / does after the student is confident.
Keep the five-slot Question Machine on screen for every task.
Give the helper card for each item in the transformation exercises.
challenge: Subject questions: compare 'Who likes Omar?' and 'Who does Omar like?' What is the difference in meaning, and why does one have does?
Question tags: 'You can swim, can't you?' Find the pattern in 4 examples.
Write 3 Shakespeare-style questions and modernize them.

successCriteria: Makes questions with is / are / can by inversion in at least 8 of the 10 transformation items.
Chooses do or does correctly and drops the main-verb -s.
Uses the order Wh- + helper + subject + verb.
Uses rising intonation for yes/no questions and falling intonation for Wh- questions in a controlled drill.
watchFor: No inversion: Where you go? / Why he is...?
Statement order with rising tone as the only question signal: You can swim?
What means...? instead of What does ... mean?

teacherNotes: Questions are the main place where English changes the strict S-V-O order taught in Bonus Class 2. Say this explicitly: 'English is strict, but questions have their own special order.'
Declarative questions ('You can swim?') do exist in real English for surprise or checking. Do not call them 'wrong'; call them 'not the normal question'.
Subject questions (Who won?) are a challenge point only; most students are not ready to contrast subject and object questions at this level.
Bonus Class 4 uses the same helpers (am / is / are) in the present continuous: Are you studying? What is she doing?

deck.title: Lumi's mystery box
deck.big: Is it big?  Can you eat it?
deck.text: Ask yes/no questions only. The teacher answers yes or no. Find the mystery object!
deck.ar: اسأل أسئلة جوابها نعم أو لا فقط، واكتشف الشيء الغامض!

deck.title: Statement -> question: what moved, and where?
deck.note: The helper (is, are, can) jumps over the subject. A Wh- word goes at the very front.
deck.noteAr: الفعل المساعد يقفز فوق الفاعل، وأداة الاستفهام تأتي في البداية.

deck.title: The Question Machine: five slots
deck.note: What + can + Omar + bake? Now fix our warm-up: It is big? -> Is it big?
deck.noteAr: ماذا + الفعل المساعد + الفاعل + الفعل. أصلح أسئلة الإحماء باستعمال الآلة.

deck.instructions: Move the helper in front of the subject. (Wh- word in brackets)
deck.instructionsAr: كوّن سؤالاً بنقل الفعل المساعد قبل الفاعل. (أداة الاستفهام بين القوسين)

items.answer: Are they in the science lab?

deck.big: You like riddles.  ->  Do you like riddles?
bullets: Like you riddles? Sounds like Shakespeare!
Sara plays tennis.  ->  Does Sara play tennis?
Only one -s: does takes it, play goes back to normal.
Where do you hang out?  What does Hamad collect?
deck.ar: إذا لم يوجد فعل مساعد نستدعي do أو does، وتنتقل -s من الفعل إلى does.

deck.instructions: Say the subject. Does it need do or does?
deck.instructionsAr: انطق الفاعل: هل يحتاج إلى do أم does؟

deck.instructions: Make a question with is, are, can, do or does. Watch the -s!
deck.instructionsAr: كوّن سؤالاً باستعمال is أو are أو can أو do أو does، وانتبه لحرف -s!

deck.noteAr: أداة الاستفهام هي الأكثر انتشاراً في العالم، واستدعاء do في الإنجليزية نادر.

deck.title: English didn't always use do
deck.text: About 400 years ago, in Shakespeare's time, people could still ask 'What say you?' or 'Know you the way?'. Over the next century or so, do became the normal helper.
deck.ar: قبل نحو 400 سنة كان الناس يسألون أحياناً بدون do، ثم صارت do هي الفعل المساعد المعتاد.

deck.instructions: Particle, intonation or word order? For old questions, say the modern one.
deck.instructionsAr: أداة استفهام أم نغمة أم ترتيب؟ وللأسئلة القديمة قل السؤال الحديث.

items.prompt: Chinese: Ni hao ma? (You good ma?)
Shakespeare's time: Know you the answer?

deck.ribbon: Arabic bridge · هل vs the machine
deck.title: Arabic adds هل. English moves the helper.
rows: do: no meaning of its own, like هل
no verb in Arabic: add is
who is the subject: no do
deck.note: Arabic keeps the statement order. English changes it.
deck.noteAr: العربية تحافظ على ترتيب الجملة الخبرية، أما الإنجليزية فتغيّره.

cards.head: Yes/no questions

cards.ar: سؤال نعم أو لا: يرتفع الصوت غالباً

bullets: Categories: Can-Do · Crew Facts · Mystery · Race Day

deck.ribbon: Did you know · kids do it too
deck.text: Young children learning English as their first language also say 'Where you going?' and 'Why he is sad?' for a while. Some of your mistakes are a natural step!
deck.ar: الأطفال الصغار الذين يتعلمون الإنجليزية لغةً أولى يقعون في الأخطاء نفسها لفترة. إنها خطوة طبيعية!

homeworkMissions.intro: Six missions to test your Question Machine. Finish them all to earn your Question Master badge!
homeworkMissions.introAr: ست مهمات لاختبار آلة الأسئلة. أنهِها كلها لتحصل على شارة سيّد الأسئلة!

missions.title: Pick the Helper
missions.intro: Which helper makes a correct question: is, are, do or does?
missions.introAr: أي فعل مساعد يكوّن سؤالاً صحيحاً: is أو are أو do أو does؟

rounds.say: Do your cousins live near school?

missions.title: Broken or Perfect?
missions.intro: Is the question correct? True = perfect, False = broken.
missions.introAr: هل السؤال صحيح؟ صح = سليم، خطأ = مكسور.

items.why: The machine needs do: Where do you go after school?
does takes the -s: Does she play tennis?
he needs does: Does he like puzzles?
Add does: What does riddle mean?
who is the subject here, so there is no do.

items.q: Why the new kid is nervous?
items.why: The helper jumps: Why is the new kid nervous?

missions.title: Up or Down?

missions.introAr: أجرِ مقابلة بالإنجليزية مع أحد أفراد أسرتك!

steps.en: Ask 5 questions: one with is, one with can, one with do, one with does, one Wh-.
steps.ar: اسأل 5 أسئلة: واحد بـ is وواحد بـ can وواحد بـ do وواحد بـ does وسؤال Wh-.

steps.en: Write the questions and their answers in your notebook.
Choose a mystery object for a 20 Questions game in the next lesson.
steps.ar: اختر شيئاً غامضاً للعبة العشرين سؤالاً في الدرس القادم.
